subject: Aurora-13b 503 Spike — coordinated mitigation & RCA next steps
body:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightai.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: BrightAI SRE Team <support@brightai.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Aurora-13b — sudden 5xx spike impacting inference pipelines

Hi Aditya,

We're seeing a sudden spike of 5xx responses and timeouts against aurora-13b since ~07:55 UTC. Traffic pattern is our normal production RT requests (ctx ~2k tokens). Error rate climbed from ~0.4% to ~8% across east-us-1 nodes. Attached is a Grafana snapshot and a short list of example request IDs (req-1182, req-1199, req-1204).

Immediate impact: two microservices retry aggressively and are hitting downstream rate limits; customers are experiencing delayed responses and increased latency. We've opened a PagerDuty incident (PD-98234). Can you confirm whether this is a known regression on your side or if we should apply a model fallback?

Thanks — Samantha
Samantha Lee
SRE Lead, BrightAI

---

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightai.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:28:05 +0000
Subject: Re: Aurora-13b — sudden 5xx spike impacting inference pipelines

Thanks for the heads up, Samantha — we see the spike on our end as well (correlates to the same request IDs). I'm escalating to infra now (cc'd Marcus) and looping in CS (Neha) to coordinate customer comms.

Immediate plan (T+0):
- Marcus to collect node-level logs and check recent runtime/kernel rollouts.
- We'll enable a temporary routing rule to route BrightAI traffic to a stable runtime group (fallback to aurora-13b:v20270420) while we investigate.
- We'll keep you posted within 20 minutes.

I've opened internal ticket RDW-321 and linked your PagerDuty. Apologies for the disruption — we take these seriously.

— Aditya
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightai.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:05:22 +0000
Subject: Re: Aurora-13b — sudden 5xx spike impacting inference pipelines

Quick update: we reproduced increased 5xx originating from a small subset of pods in us-east-1. Symptoms: failed kernel selection on long-context requests -> fallback attempted and then exhausted, producing 502/503. Root suspect: an automated kernel-selection rollout that completed at 07:48 UTC and affected ~12% of aurora-13b capacity.

Actions taken (09:00–09:10 UTC):
- Rolled back kernel-selection config to previous stable (vK-202703) for affected hosts.
- Initiated rolling restart of the impacted pods to flush stale caches.
- Applied a temporary routing policy to divert BrightAI traffic to the unaffected capacity pool.

Attached: ops-log-aurora13b-20270514.txt (truncated) with trace IDs. We're monitoring; initial error rate is falling but not fully back to baseline.

— Marcus
Infra Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

---

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightai.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:40:10 +0000
Subject: Re: Aurora-13b — sudden 5xx spike impacting inference pipelines

Samantha — thanks for your patience.

Status (11:40 UTC):
- We've applied the routing rule so BrightAI requests are served from the stable runtime pool.
- Overall 5xx rate for aurora-13b has fallen from peak ~8% to ~0.6% on your traffic.
- Marcus's team completed rolling restarts and kernel rollback for the affected hosts. We've kept the previous kernel in the stable pool while we finish logs and a short postmortem.

Next steps:
1) We'll produce a short RCA and a set of mitigations by EOD today.
2) If you prefer, we can schedule an immediate permanent pin of your tenant to the stable runtime until the fix is validated (requires brief maintenance window).
3) As a courtesy for the disruption, we're prepared to issue a service credit for the affected window after the RCA.

Can you confirm whether BrightAI observed any residual errors after 11:15 UTC? If you can share sample request traces that still show errors, please include them.

— Aditya

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightai.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Aurora-13b incident (PD-98234) — RCA and remediation plan

Hi Samantha — following up with the RCA and next steps after our initial mitigation. Thanks again for the quick signal and for working with our ops team during the incident.

Summary: 2027-05-14 07:48 UTC — automated kernel-selection rollout (vK-202305 -> vK-202310) introduced an edge-case where the kernel chooser selected an optimization path incompatible with long-context KV cache warmup for a subset of inference requests. This caused repeated kernel fallback attempts and resulted in elevated 5xx/timeout rates on ~12% of aurora-13b capacity.

Impact: BrightAI observed increased 5xx and request timeouts between 07:55–09:45 UTC (peak 8% error rate). We estimate BrightAI traffic experienced degraded success for approximately 1h 50m.

Root cause: insufficient canary isolation for the kernel-selection rollout combined with a regression in fallback handling that retried fallback paths synchronously rather than using backoff, saturating request handling on affected pods.

Remediation completed on 2027-05-14:
- Immediate rollback of kernel-selection config on affected hosts.
- Rolling restart of impacted pods to clear mismatched KV caches.
- Temporary routing rule to divert BrightAI to stable runtime pool.

Planned follow-ups (commit schedule):
- RDW-321 (JIRA) — add stronger canary gating and add binary flag to decouple kernel-selection rollout from customer-facing pools (ETA: 2027-05-21).
- Improve fallback backoff logic to avoid synchronous retry storms (ETA: 2027-06-04).
- Add request-level health checks so we fail fast to alternative model variants instead of retrying on the same node (ETA: 2027-06-11).

Customer options and next steps:
- We can permanently pin BrightAI to the stable aurora-13b runtime until the remediation is validated. This requires a maintenance window (10–20 minutes) during which we will shift traffic. Please let us know preferred date/times.
- As noted, we'll apply a pro-rated service credit for the affected window; finance will follow up with a credit memo once you confirm the impacted usage window.

Attachments: RCA summary PDF, ops logs, grafana snapshot (all attached). PagerDuty incident PD-98234 closed.

Links: PagerDuty PD-98234, JIRA RDW-321, Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/aurora/aurora13b-503s-snapshot

If you have questions or want a tech-ops call to walk through traces, we're available tomorrow between 14:00–18:00 UTC.

Thanks again — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
